catalog_phase: Phase 2 - Core evidence sources, gaps closed against Microsoft Learn
notes: Single source of truth for Poster 1, Poster 2 and the interactive site. Every URL is referenced by source id (data/sources.json). An entry is 'Verified' only when verification.gaps is empty; 'Conditional' entries list exactly what is still unconfirmed.

entries.description: Directory audit trail of tasks performed in the tenant by users, applications, and services, including changes to users, groups, applications, licenses, and other directory objects.
entries.configuration_notes: Generated without configuration. Routing to a Log Analytics workspace, Azure Storage account, or Event Hubs requires a Microsoft Entra diagnostic setting; Security Administrator is the least-privileged role to configure one.
entries.licensing_dependency: Native retention is 7 days with Microsoft Entra ID Free and 30 days with P1 or P2. Audit logs are available for the features the tenant has licensed.
entries.where_to_investigate: Microsoft Entra admin center; Microsoft Graph audit logs API; Log Analytics (AuditLogs) when routed by a diagnostic setting.
entries.portal_path: Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Monitoring & health
preservation_options: Microsoft Entra diagnostic setting to a Log Analytics workspace
Microsoft Entra diagnostic setting to an Azure Storage account (archive)
Microsoft Entra diagnostic setting to Event Hubs
Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) retention for Microsoft Entra audit records (E5-class or Purview Suite licensing)
Download from the portal as CSV or JSON
entries.native_retention: 7 days (Microsoft Entra ID Free); 30 days (Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2)
entries.retention_notes: Retention changes are not retroactive: after an upgrade from Free to P1 or P2, only data still inside the 7-day window is available. Retention at a routed destination is governed by that destination.
investigation_relevance: Who granted a user membership in an administrative group, and when
What changes were made to an application or service principal
How many password resets were made in a period
What operations a specific agent identity performed

commands.purpose: Authenticate with the permissions needed to read activity logs.
commands.notes: Add Policy.Read.ConditionalAccess when Conditional Access details are needed.

commands.purpose: Retrieve directory audit records.
commands.pagination: -All follows every page; -Top and -PageSize bound the result. activityDateTime supports eq, ge, and le in $filter, and $orderby.
commands.notes: Other documented filters: activityDisplayName (eq, startswith), correlationId (eq), loggedByService (eq), initiatedBy/user/id, initiatedBy/user/userPrincipalName, and initiatedBy/app/appId.

api.name: Microsoft Graph (audit logs API)
api.notes: Available in the global service and national clouds. Custom security attribute audit logs and provisioning logs are available only on the beta endpoint.

required_permissions.value: AuditLog.Read.All (least privileged); Directory.Read.All (higher privileged)
AuditLog.Read.All (least privileged); Directory.Read.All (higher privileged)
Reports Reader (least privileged), Security Reader, or Security Administrator to read audit logs
Attribute Log Reader or Attribute Log Administrator for custom security attribute audit logs
Security Administrator (least privileged to configure Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings)

limitations: Native retention is 7 or 30 days. Without a diagnostic setting in place before the incident, older records cannot be recovered.
Custom security attribute audit logs and provisioning logs are only on the Microsoft Graph beta endpoint.
Audit logs are available only for features the tenant has licensed.
The IP address in an audit record is the OAuth client's IP address (the TCP peer of the service endpoint), not necessarily the end user's device.

kql_examples.title: Coverage check: oldest and newest AuditLogs records in the workspace
kql_examples.query:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(3653d)
| summarize OldestAuditEvent=min(TimeGenerated), NewestAuditEvent=max(TimeGenerated) by Type

entries.description: Records of sign-in attempts by users and client applications, split into four types: interactive user, non-interactive user, service principal, and managed identity sign-ins. Each record includes status, client, application, location, and Conditional Access details.
entries.configuration_notes: Generated without configuration. Each sign-in type is a separate diagnostic-setting category (SignInLogs, NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs, ServicePrincipalSignInLogs, ManagedIdentitySignInLogs); each one must be selected to be routed.
entries.licensing_dependency: Native retention is 7 days with Microsoft Entra ID Free and 30 days with P1 or P2. Querying sign-ins through Microsoft Graph requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license on the tenant.
entries.where_to_investigate: Microsoft Entra admin center; Microsoft Graph /auditLogs/signIns; Log Analytics sign-in tables when routed.
entries.portal_path: Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs
preservation_options: Microsoft Entra diagnostic setting to a Log Analytics workspace (select each sign-in category)
Microsoft Entra diagnostic setting to an Azure Storage account (archive)
Microsoft Entra diagnostic setting to Event Hubs
entries.native_retention: 7 days (Microsoft Entra ID Free); 30 days (Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2)
entries.retention_notes: Retention changes are not retroactive after a license upgrade. The List signIns API returns only sign-ins within the default retention period.

log_analytics_tables.notes: Interactive user sign-ins. ResultType 0 indicates success.

investigation_relevance: Sign-in pattern of a user: when, from where, with which client and application
Whether sign-ins succeeded or failed, and which Conditional Access policies applied
Non-interactive sign-ins made by clients on behalf of a user
Service principal and managed identity authentication activity

commands.purpose: Authenticate with the permissions needed to read sign-in logs.
commands.notes: Directory.Read.All is needed alongside AuditLog.Read.All to avoid intermittent premium-license errors.

commands.purpose: Retrieve interactive user sign-ins for a bounded time window.
commands.pagination: Maximum and default page size is 1,000; most recent first. Filter on a time range to avoid timeouts.
commands.notes: The v1.0 API returns interactive user sign-ins (and successful federated sign-ins) only.

commands.example: Get-MgBetaAuditLogSignIn -Filter "(createdDateTime ge 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z and createdDateTime le 2026-10-07T23:59:59Z) and signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'nonInteractiveUser')"
commands.purpose: Retrieve non-interactive user sign-ins. Use 'servicePrincipal' or 'managedIdentity' in the filter for those sign-in types.
commands.notes: Beta APIs are subject to change and aren't supported for production. Without an event-type filter the API returns interactive user sign-ins only.

api.name: Microsoft Graph
api.notes: Non-interactive, service principal and managed identity sign-ins are retrieved from the beta endpoint with a signInEventTypes filter.

required_permissions.value: AuditLog.Read.All (least privileged); add Directory.Read.All to avoid intermittent license-check errors
Policy.Read.ConditionalAccess (or Policy.Read.All) to receive appliedConditionalAccessPolicies
Global Reader, Reports Reader, Security Administrator, Security Operator, or Security Reader (delegated access)

limitations: Without a signInEventTypes filter, the List signIns API returns only interactive user sign-ins; the other three types require the beta endpoint.
Only sign-ins within the Microsoft Entra default retention period are available through the API.
appliedConditionalAccessPolicies is omitted when the caller cannot read Conditional Access data.
Each sign-in type is a separate diagnostic-setting category; routing only SignInLogs leaves the other three types uncollected.

kql_examples.title: Coverage check: time range held for non-interactive sign-ins

gaps: Page size and limits of the beta signIns endpoint (non-interactive, service principal, and managed identity sign-ins) are not confirmed.

entries.description: Record of Azure management (control-plane) operations on resources, such as create, update, delete, and action operations, plus Resource Manager deployment errors. It does not typically capture read operations, and it is not a record of operations performed inside a resource.
entries.configuration_notes: Collected by default with no configuration. A diagnostic setting (Export Activity Logs) is required to keep entries beyond 90 days or to query them in Log Analytics. A management-group diagnostic setting covers the hierarchy below it and can duplicate subscription-level exports.
entries.where_to_investigate: Azure portal Activity log (Monitor, subscription, resource group, or resource); Activity Log REST API; Log Analytics (AzureActivity) when exported.
preservation_options: Diagnostic setting to a Log Analytics workspace (AzureActivity table; retention up to 12 years)
Diagnostic setting to an Azure Storage account (insights-activity-logs container, hourly PT1H.json blobs)
Diagnostic setting to Event Hubs
Download from the portal as CSV
entries.native_retention: 90 days
entries.retention_notes: There are no ingestion charges for activity logs in Log Analytics; retention charges apply only past 90 days. The Activity Log is the only place that stores the creator of a resource, so exporting it is how creator information is kept beyond 90 days.

log_analytics_tables.notes: Structure varies by event category. Use case-insensitive comparisons.

investigation_relevance: Who created, changed, or deleted an Azure resource, and when
Changes made through Azure Resource Manager, such as a key vault access policy change
Which identity initiated a management operation (caller, claims, authorization, caller IP address)
Deployment errors and operations that share a correlation ID
Role assignment and custom role definition changes, recorded in the Administrative category

commands.purpose: Retrieve subscription-level events (subscription from the current Az context) for a time range.
commands.pagination: Microsoft's examples return at most 1,000 events per call; narrow the time range or set -MaxRecord. Both ends of the range must fall inside the 90-day retention window.
commands.notes: Parameter sets scope by subscription (default), -ResourceGroupName, -ResourceId, -ResourceProvider, or -CorrelationId; -Caller and -Status filter further; -DetailedOutput returns full properties. Microsoft's examples export with Export-Csv; JSON keeps nested claims and properties intact.

commands.example: Invoke-AzRestMethod -Method GET -Path "/providers/Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes/management/values?api-version=2015-04-01&`$filter=eventTimestamp ge '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' and eventTimestamp le '2026-10-07T23:59:59Z'"
commands.purpose: Retrieve tenant-level events, which have no dedicated cmdlet.
commands.notes: Tenant-level events are separate from subscription events and can include management group or subscription creation.

commands.example: Invoke-AzRestMethod -Method GET -Path "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<managementGroupId>/providers/Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes/management/values?api-version=2017-03-01-preview&`$filter=eventTimestamp ge '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' and eventTimestamp le '2026-10-07T23:59:59Z'"
commands.purpose: Retrieve management-group-level events (policy assignments, membership changes).
commands.notes: Microsoft documents the 2017-03-01-preview API version as required for management-group queries.

api.name: Activity Log REST API (Azure Resource Manager)
api.notes: A $filter with at least an eventTimestamp start value is required. Maximum client timeout is 75 seconds (Prefer: wait=75).

required_permissions.value: Monitoring Reader (can query the Activity Log). A custom role with Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes/* limits access to Activity Log reads.

limitations: Retained for 90 days natively; both ends of a query time range must fall inside that window.
Does not typically capture read operations. Operations inside a resource are in Resource Logs.
Tenant- and management-group-level scopes only capture Azure Resource Manager events in those hierarchies.
Values in AzureActivity fields can differ in case; use case-insensitive operators.
Entries are usually available 3 to 20 minutes after the event.
The Activity Log REST API is limited to 50 queries per 30 seconds with a 75-second maximum timeout; querying AzureActivity in a workspace counts against the general Logs query limits instead.

kql_examples.title: Count of activity log records per category
Remove duplicates collected at several scopes
kql_examples.query:
AzureActivity
| extend Hash = hash(dynamic_to_json(pack_all()))
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by Hash

gaps: Paging of the Activity Log REST API at tenant and management-group scope (continuation or nextLink handling) is not confirmed.

entries.description: Per-resource logs of operations performed within an Azure resource, such as getting a secret from a key vault or making a request to a database. Content and categories differ by resource type. Azure resources generate Resource Logs, but Azure Monitor does not collect them by default. A Diagnostic Setting or another documented collection configuration must exist for historical collection.
entries.configuration_notes: Create a diagnostic setting for each resource and select the categories to collect. Resource Logs aren't collected or stored until a diagnostic setting routes them. Older documentation calls these 'diagnostic logs'; Microsoft now calls them Resource Logs.
entries.where_to_investigate: The destination chosen in the resource's diagnostic setting: Log Analytics workspace, Azure Storage account, Event Hubs, or a partner integration.
preservation_options: Log Analytics workspace (table retention up to 12 years total)
Azure Storage account (insights-logs-{category} containers, hourly PT1H.json blobs); an immutability policy prevents modification
Event Hubs
Azure Monitor partner integrations
entries.native_retention: None: not collected or stored by Azure Monitor unless a diagnostic setting routes them
entries.retention_notes: Retention is set at the destination: Log Analytics table retention, or the storage account's own lifecycle settings.

log_analytics_tables.notes: Legacy collection mode used by a minority of services. Most services write to resource-specific tables, one per category; see the per-service entries and the supported categories reference.

investigation_relevance: Data-plane activity inside a resource that the Activity Log does not record
Request-level detail (caller, operation, result) for resource types whose schema includes it

commands.purpose: Query Resource Logs already routed to a Log Analytics workspace. After switching a setting to resource-specific mode, earlier data stays in AzureDiagnostics, so query both with union.
commands.pagination: No paging. Logs query API limits: 500,000 records and about 100 MB per query, 10-minute maximum run time (3-minute default), 200 requests per 30 seconds per user. Split large pulls by time range.
commands.notes: Replace the placeholder with the service's resource-specific table from the supported categories reference.

api.name: Azure Monitor Logs query API
api.notes: Applies when the logs are routed to a Log Analytics workspace. The JSON body takes query, an optional ISO 8601 timespan, and optional workspaces for cross-workspace queries. v1 is part of the path; there is no api-version parameter.

required_permissions.value: Monitoring Reader (can search Log Analytics workspaces and run log queries)

limitations: Not completely lossless: store-and-forward with retries but no transactional guarantees, so small losses can occur.
Ingestion latency varies by destination and service.
AzureDiagnostics is not the universal table. Most services write to resource-specific tables, and some let you choose the mode.
Storage blobs are named by the time records were received, so a blob can contain records outside the hour in its path.
Monitoring Reader and Monitoring Contributor don't grant read access to log data in storage accounts or Event Hubs; reading an archived copy needs separate data access.
Data starts flowing up to 90 minutes after a diagnostic setting is created; nothing is collected for the period before it existed.
entries.notes: Poster 1 points readers to the official supported categories reference instead of printing every category. Per-service categories are separate catalog entries.

entries.description: A collection and routing configuration, not an evidence source. It decides which Resource Log categories, platform metrics, or Activity Log entries go to a Log Analytics workspace, Azure Storage account, Event Hubs, or partner solution. Whether a setting existed at the time of an incident decides whether Resource Logs exist at all.
entries.configuration_notes: A diagnostic setting names the categories (or a category group: allLogs, or audit for logs that record interactions with data or service settings) and up to one destination of each type: Log Analytics workspace, Azure Storage account, Event Hubs, or a partner solution. Each resource can have up to five diagnostic settings. Storage and Event Hubs destinations must be in the same region as a regional resource. Activity Log export is a subscription-scope setting created with an ARM template or the portal, not with New-AzDiagnosticSetting.
entries.where_to_investigate: Azure portal (resource > Diagnostic settings); Az PowerShell; Microsoft Entra admin center for Microsoft Entra logs.
entries.portal_path: Azure portal > resource > Diagnostic settings; Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Diagnostic settings
entries.native_retention: Not applicable (configuration object)
entries.retention_notes: Each destination in the setting determines how long the routed data is kept.
investigation_relevance: Whether a resource's logs were being collected, which categories, and to which destination; establish this before concluding that missing logs mean no activity
Which collection mode (AzureDiagnostics or resource-specific) applies, and therefore which tables to query

commands.purpose: Record the diagnostic settings currently active on a resource.
commands.notes: Returns the active (current) settings, not their history.

commands.purpose: List the log and metric categories a resource supports.
Create a diagnostic setting (forensic readiness or containment).
commands.notes: Changes the environment. Record who ran it and when. It does not create logs for activity that happened before it existed.

api.name: Azure Resource Manager (Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings)
api.endpoint: Extension resource Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings on the monitored resource (REST operation: Diagnostic Settings - Create Or Update)
api.notes: ARM templates and Bicep deploy the same resource type; Activity Log settings are deployed at subscription scope.

required_permissions.value: Monitoring Reader to view diagnostic settings; Monitoring Contributor to create or edit them, plus ListKeys on a storage account or Event Hubs destination. Read access to the resource type and scope is also needed.
Security Administrator (least privileged to configure Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings)

limitations: Shows current configuration only; on its own it does not prove what was configured at the time of an incident.
Some services need more than one diagnostic setting to collect both legacy and resource-specific logs (for example, Azure Firewall).
Switching an existing setting to resource-specific mode leaves earlier data in AzureDiagnostics.
Data starts flowing up to 90 minutes after a setting is created.

If a resource is deleted or renamed and later re-created with the same name, a leftover diagnostic setting can apply to the new resource and resume collection. Microsoft advises deleting diagnostic settings with the resource.
Diagnostic settings don't allow filtering within a category; transformations filter supported tables in the workspace.

gaps: Whether creating, changing, or deleting a diagnostic setting is recorded in the Azure Activity Log is not stated in the documentation reviewed. This decides how historical collection state can be established.

entries.description: Numeric time-series values collected automatically from Azure resources at regular intervals. Supporting operational and timeline context, not an audit trail.
entries.configuration_notes: No configuration and no ingestion or storage cost. Some platform metrics can be routed to Log Analytics with a diagnostic setting; check each metric's export setting.
entries.where_to_investigate: Azure portal metrics explorer; Az PowerShell; Log Analytics (AzureMetrics) when routed.
preservation_options: Diagnostic setting to a Log Analytics workspace for long-term trending
Metrics export using data collection rules
entries.native_retention: 93 days (platform and custom metrics)
entries.retention_notes: A single chart queries up to 30 days; pan to reach the full 93 days. Moving or renaming a resource may lose its metric history. Azure doesn't collect metrics for stopped virtual machines.
investigation_relevance: When request volume, errors, or throughput on a resource changed
Corroborating the time window suggested by audit or resource logs

commands.purpose: Retrieve metric values for a resource and time range.
commands.notes: Supported metric names are listed in the Azure Monitor supported metrics reference.

api.name: Azure Monitor Metrics REST API (Azure Resource Manager)
api.notes: A Metrics Batch REST API retrieves metrics for up to 50 resource IDs in the same subscription and region in one call. Not every metric is exportable by diagnostic settings; multidimensional metrics are flattened when exported.

required_permissions.value: Monitoring Reader (can query metrics); read access to the resource type and scope

limitations: Numeric aggregates only; no identity or request detail.
Cannot query more than 93 days back.
Some resources emit metrics only when activity occurs, so an empty chart can mean no qualifying events.

entries.description: Resource log of authentication API requests to a key vault and of operations on the vault and its keys, secrets, and certificates, recording who made each request and when.
entries.configuration_notes: Enable a diagnostic setting on the vault with the AuditEvent category (in the portal, category groups 'audit' and 'allLogs').
entries.where_to_investigate: The destination of the vault's diagnostic setting: Log Analytics workspace, Azure Storage account, or Event Hubs.
entries.portal_path: Azure portal > key vault > Diagnostic settings
preservation_options: Diagnostic setting to a Log Analytics workspace
Diagnostic setting to an Azure Storage account
Diagnostic setting to Event Hubs
entries.native_retention: None: not collected or stored until a diagnostic setting routes them
entries.retention_notes: Retention is set at the destination.

log_analytics_tables.notes: Azure Policy evaluation details.
Azure Key Vault is listed among services that use Azure diagnostics mode.

investigation_relevance: Which identity accessed or tried to access a secret, key, or certificate, and when
Changes to the vault, its access policies, keys, and secrets
Authentication API requests made to the vault

commands.purpose: Query Key Vault audit events routed to Log Analytics. Also check AzureDiagnostics, which holds Key Vault data collected in Azure diagnostics mode.
commands.pagination: No paging. Logs query API limits: 500,000 records and about 100 MB per query, 10-minute maximum run time (3-minute default), 200 requests per 30 seconds per user. Split large pulls by time range.

api.name: Azure Monitor Logs query API
api.notes: Applies when the logs are routed to a Log Analytics workspace. The JSON body takes query, an optional ISO 8601 timespan, and optional workspaces for cross-workspace queries. v1 is part of the path; there is no api-version parameter.

required_permissions.value: Monitoring Reader (can search Log Analytics workspaces and run log queries)

limitations: Key Vault documentation calls AuditEvent the only Key Vault log category, while the Log Analytics table reference also lists a policy-evaluation table. Confirm the categories with Get-AzDiagnosticSettingCategory.
Key Vault documentation examples use Set-AzDiagnosticSetting, while the current Az.Monitor reference documents New-AzDiagnosticSetting. Check against the installed Az.Monitor version.
Key Vault appears in the AzureDiagnostics-mode service list and also has resource-specific tables; check both.
Monitoring Reader and Monitoring Contributor don't grant read access to log data in storage accounts or Event Hubs; reading an archived copy needs separate data access.

gaps: Key Vault documentation and the AzureDiagnostics table reference say Key Vault writes to AzureDiagnostics, while the Log Analytics table reference lists resource-specific Key Vault tables. Whether a collection-mode selector is offered for Key Vault is not confirmed; query both.

entries.notes: Key Vault access-policy changes made through Azure Resource Manager also appear in the Azure Activity Log.

entries.description: Per-request resource logs for the Blob, File, Queue, and Table services. Records successful and failed requests and how each request was authorized: Microsoft Entra ID, Shared Key, shared access signature (SAS), or anonymous.
entries.configuration_notes: Configure diagnostic settings on the account and on each data service (blob, file, queue, table) to be covered. Classic Storage Analytics logging (the $logs container) is a separate legacy mechanism; Microsoft recommends Azure Monitor resource logs instead.
entries.where_to_investigate: The destination of each service's diagnostic setting: Log Analytics workspace, Azure Storage account, or Event Hubs.
entries.portal_path: Azure portal > storage account > Diagnostic settings
preservation_options: Diagnostic setting to a Log Analytics workspace
Diagnostic setting to a separate Azure Storage account
Diagnostic setting to Event Hubs
entries.native_retention: None: not collected or stored until a diagnostic setting routes them
entries.retention_notes: Retention is set at the destination.

log_analytics_tables.notes: Categories StorageRead, StorageWrite, StorageDelete.

investigation_relevance: Which principal or token read, wrote, or deleted data, and when
How requests were authorized, including unexpected Shared Key, SAS, or anonymous access
Failed requests: authorization, throttling, network, and time-out errors

commands.purpose: Query storage request logs routed to Log Analytics.
commands.pagination: No paging. Logs query API limits: 500,000 records and about 100 MB per query, 10-minute maximum run time (3-minute default), 200 requests per 30 seconds per user. Split large pulls by time range.

api.name: Azure Monitor Logs query API
api.notes: Applies when the logs are routed to a Log Analytics workspace. The JSON body takes query, an optional ISO 8601 timespan, and optional workspaces for cross-workspace queries. v1 is part of the path; there is no api-version parameter.

required_permissions.value: Monitoring Reader (can search Log Analytics workspaces and run log queries)

limitations: Requests are logged on a best-effort basis.
Of failed anonymous requests, only server errors, time-outs, and 304 (Not Modified) GET failures are logged.
Requests made by the Blob service itself, such as log creation or deletion, aren't logged. Azure Monitor filters out activity in 'insights-logs-' containers.
Operations the Azure portal performs while someone views the account are also logged.
Monitoring Reader and Monitoring Contributor don't grant read access to log data in storage accounts or Event Hubs; reading an archived copy needs separate data access.

entries.description: Resource logs of each connection that matches a network, application, or NAT rule, plus threat-intelligence hits, IDPS signature hits, DNS proxy queries, and optional flow trace data.
entries.configuration_notes: Requires a diagnostic setting. Structured (resource-specific) logs and legacy (AzureDiagnostics) logs need at least two diagnostic settings if both are wanted. DNS proxy logs exist only when DNS proxy is enabled on the firewall. Which events can exist depends on the SKU: IDPS is a Premium feature, and Basic supports threat intelligence in alert mode only.
entries.where_to_investigate: The destination of the firewall's diagnostic setting; Log Analytics resource-specific AZFW* tables.
preservation_options: Diagnostic setting to a Log Analytics workspace (resource-specific mode recommended)
Diagnostic setting to an Azure Storage account
Diagnostic setting to Event Hubs
entries.native_retention: None: not collected or stored until a diagnostic setting routes them
entries.retention_notes: Retention is set at the destination.

log_analytics_tables.notes: Legacy application rule, network rule, and DNS proxy categories; details are in a free-text message.

investigation_relevance: Whether traffic between a source and destination was allowed or denied, and by which rule
Outbound application (FQDN) access through the firewall
Threat-intelligence and IDPS signature matches
DNS queries handled by the firewall's DNS proxy

commands.example: Invoke-AzOperationalInsightsQuery -WorkspaceId <workspace-id> -Query "AZFWNetworkRule | union AZFWApplicationRule, AZFWNatRule, AZFWThreatIntel, AZFWIdpsSignature" -Timespan (New-TimeSpan -Days 7)
commands.purpose: Retrieve firewall decisions routed to Log Analytics.
commands.pagination: No paging. Logs query API limits: 500,000 records and about 100 MB per query, 10-minute maximum run time (3-minute default), 200 requests per 30 seconds per user. Split large pulls by time range.

api.name: Azure Monitor Logs query API
api.notes: Applies when the logs are routed to a Log Analytics workspace. The JSON body takes query, an optional ISO 8601 timespan, and optional workspaces for cross-workspace queries. v1 is part of the path; there is no api-version parameter.

required_permissions.value: Monitoring Reader (can search Log Analytics workspaces and run log queries)

limitations: Legacy AzureDiagnostics categories put details in a free-text properties message; resource-specific tables are structured.
Firewall logs cover traffic that passes through the firewall only.
Monitoring Reader and Monitoring Contributor don't grant read access to log data in storage accounts or Event Hubs; reading an archived copy needs separate data access.

kql_examples.title: All firewall decisions (network, application, NAT, threat intelligence, IDPS)
kql_examples.query:
AZFWNetworkRule
| union AZFWApplicationRule, AZFWNatRule, AZFWThreatIntel, AZFWIdpsSignature
| take 100

entries.description: Network Watcher logs of IP traffic through a virtual network, subnet, or network interface (flow tuple, allowed or denied, bytes and packets), written to an Azure Storage account. Successor to NSG flow logs.
entries.configuration_notes: Create a flow log on the virtual network, subnet, or network interface and choose a storage account. Traffic analytics is a separate, optional setting that processes flow logs into a Log Analytics workspace every 10 or 60 minutes.
entries.where_to_investigate: Azure Storage account (raw flow logs); Log Analytics NTANetAnalytics (traffic analytics output).
entries.portal_path: Azure portal > Network Watcher > Logs > Flow logs
preservation_options: Storage account retention set on the flow log (Standard general-purpose v2 accounts)
Traffic analytics to a Log Analytics workspace
entries.native_retention: Set per flow log in days on Standard general-purpose v2 storage accounts; 0 keeps data until manually deleted
entries.retention_notes: Traffic analytics output in Log Analytics follows the workspace table retention.

log_analytics_tables.notes: Traffic analytics output: aggregated and enriched per processing interval, not raw flow records. Replaces AzureNetworkAnalytics_CL used with NSG flow logs.

investigation_relevance: Whether a connection between two IP addresses and ports occurred, and whether it was allowed or denied
Bytes and packets per flow, including stateless flows
Traffic to private endpoints, recorded at the source VM
Which network security group or security admin rule allowed or denied a flow

commands.purpose: Query traffic analytics output when traffic analytics was enabled.
commands.pagination: No paging; Azure Monitor log query limits apply.
commands.notes: Use only SubType FlowLog; other values are internal.

commands.purpose: Download raw virtual network flow-log blobs (hourly PT1H.json files) from the storage account.
commands.pagination: Get-AzStorageBlob lists the blobs; Microsoft recommends -MaxCount when a container holds many blobs.
commands.notes: Blob path: insights-logs-flowlogflowevent/flowLogResourceID=/{subscriptionID}_NETWORKWATCHERRG/NETWORKWATCHER_{Region}_{ResourceName}-{ResourceGroupName}-FLOWLOGS/y=/m=/d=/h=/m=00/macAddress=/PT1H.json. Hash each downloaded file.

api.notes: Raw records are block blobs in Azure Storage.

required_permissions.value: Verification required: Network Watcher and storage account permissions (Microsoft documents a Network Watcher RBAC permissions article)

limitations: The storage account must be in the same region as the virtual network and be Standard tier.
Rotating customer-managed keys on the storage account stops flow logging until it is disabled and re-enabled.
Don't modify flow-log blobs while they are being written; it can break writes for that hour's blob.
Traffic can't be recorded at a private endpoint; it is captured at the source VM.
Outbound VM flows to ExpressRoute aren't recorded when flow logging is enabled on the ExpressRoute gateway subnet; FastPath traffic bypasses the gateway.
Azure Container Instances aren't supported.

kql_examples.title: Subnets interacting with non-Azure public IPs in the last 30 days
kql_examples.query:
NTANetAnalytics
| where SubType == "FlowLog" and FlowStartTime > ago(30d) and FlowType == "ExternalPublic"
| project SrcSubnet, DestSubnet

gaps: Raw flow-log record schema not yet catalogued.
Azure RBAC role needed to read flow-log blobs from the storage account, and Network Watcher permissions, not confirmed.

entries.notes: Network Watcher charges per GB of flow logs collected (5 GB per month free per subscription); traffic analytics is billed separately.

entries.description: Legacy Network Watcher flow logging per network security group, written to Azure Storage. New NSG flow logs can no longer be created, and the feature retires on September 30, 2027.
entries.configuration_notes: Existing NSG flow logs only. Migrate to virtual network flow logs, then turn off NSG flow logs to avoid duplicate records.
entries.where_to_investigate: Azure Storage account configured on the existing flow log; AzureNetworkAnalytics_CL if traffic analytics was enabled.
entries.portal_path: Azure portal > Network Watcher > Logs > Flow logs
preservation_options: Storage account retention configured on the flow log

entries.description: The Windows Security event channel, populated according to the device's audit policy. Depth of detail, such as process creation events with command lines, depends on which audit settings are enabled.
entries.configuration_notes: Audit categories are enabled by basic or advanced audit policy. Audit Process Creation (events 4688 and 4696) defaults to Not configured; the 'Include command line in process creation events' setting (Administrative Templates\System\Audit Process Creation, or Policy CSP ADMX_AuditSettings/IncludeCmdLine) is not enabled by default. Audit Process Termination writes 4689. If basic audit policy overwrites advanced settings, event 4719 is logged; 'Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings' prevents that. Central collection: an Azure Monitor Agent data collection rule with a Windows events data source sends the selected events to the Event table. Custom filters use the form LogName!XPath (XPath 1.0 only); test a filter locally with Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath first. Analytic and Debug channels can't be collected, and event logs must be on a local disk. The Microsoft Sentinel 'Windows Security Events via AMA' connector sends Security and AppLocker events to the SecurityEvent table instead, using the All, Common, Minimal, or Custom event set. In a data collection rule definition, the data source is windowsEventLogs, its filters are in xPathQueries, and the stream is Microsoft-Event.

entries.evidence_source: PowerShell Operational logs (script block and module logging)
entries.description: Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes to Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational and PowerShell 7 writes to PowerShellCore/Operational. With Script Block Logging enabled, PowerShell records the content of the script blocks it processes (event 4104). Module logging records pipeline execution for selected modules (event 4103).
entries.configuration_notes: Enable 'Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging' through Group Policy (Windows Components > Windows PowerShell for 5.1; Administrative Templates > PowerShell Core for 7), the policy registry key, or the MDM Policy CSP (WindowsPowerShell/TurnOnPowerShellScriptBlockLogging). On Windows, PowerShell 7 also needs its event provider registered ($PSHOME\RegisterManifest.ps1). Microsoft recommends Protected Event Logging when script block logging is used for more than diagnostics. Central collection: an Azure Monitor Agent data collection rule with a Windows events data source sends the selected events to the Event table. Custom filters use the form LogName!XPath (XPath 1.0 only); test a filter locally with Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath first. Analytic and Debug channels can't be collected, and event logs must be on a local disk. Example filter, built from the documented format: Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational!*[System[(EventID=4104)]].
entries.where_to_investigate: On the device: Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs.
entries.portal_path: Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell > Operational (5.1); PowerShellCore > Operational (7)

entries.description: Local event channel where Microsoft Defender Antivirus records scans, detections, remediation actions, and configuration changes. Continuous telemetry, distinct from the on-demand support package.
entries.configuration_notes: Written while Defender Antivirus runs. Its mode matters: in passive mode threats are reported but not remediated; when disabled or uninstalled, files aren't scanned. Get-MpComputerStatus reports the mode in AMRunningMode. Central collection: an Azure Monitor Agent data collection rule with a Windows events data source sends the selected events to the Event table. Custom filters use the form LogName!XPath (XPath 1.0 only); test a filter locally with Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath first. Analytic and Debug channels can't be collected, and event logs must be on a local disk.
